title: Segregation on the road
summary: Travelling south, they asked whether they could use gas-station bathrooms before buying gas, and had no serious incidents.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well that's the thing that you look for that book. Speaking of, I mean so you were on the road a great deal. What are some of the problems of being on the road? Being out on the road? Well just the idea that.

In that time. Well we didn't have too much of a problem. There was a lot of segregation in a lot of places but we didn't encounter too much of it. I mean when you went south we'd stop at a station and found out could you use the bathroom before you buy any gas. If they say you could use bathroom then we'd buy the gas.
So some places they'd let you.

Some places they would. Some places they wouldn't. You know so mostly in the south we ran into that type of thing. But we never encountered nothing of any serious nature. We never had any kind of, some people really ran into some things you know. But we, I can't remember any incident at all that causes any kind of trouble. That's the only thing I'm saying. We went to bathrooms or filling stations. We'd always find out could we use it before we buy it. And I remember the first time we went to Florida the lady said, if you fill up drink all orange juice you want. I used to do a lot of driving so I got out man I got my belly filled up. Then I woke up everybody else in the car, hey man y'all get some orange juice. And then we fill up and go down to Florida. They didn't do nothing but come out with another bowl and put it back on top you know. You know like the water jug you know. Put another bowl up there with the juice in it. Ready for business for whoever else coming in there. But other than that no. We never encountered too much of anything.
